This is such a simple but addictive game. 

Recommendations:
1. Being able to see my inventory in the computer while ordering 
2. Customize my workers and be able to upgrade them to work faster
3. Be able to order more than 10 items at a time
4. Online Mode!!! (would love to play this game with my friends)
5. A way to see what the customers are saying about prices or out of stocks
6. Being able to move items on shelves without using a box 
7. Maybe a grid while putting up lights or shelves my OCD cant take it anymore lol
8. I need a worker turn off switch so I don't have to fire every time I rearrange my store.
9. Higher end products I get its a grocery store but so is Walmart and Target and they have stuff other than food. 
10. Rotate storage inventory annoying when I order and the full box gets put in front of a half stored box. 

I know your working hard on making a fantastic game. Keep up the great work! And for anyone on the fence on getting this game it is most definitely worth it.

Hands down my favorite feature. the customization is finally here as well. Paint your walls, change the floors, name your store its all here and makes it feel like my own store. I just want to tell the developer and his team your doing a fantastic job and I see and appreciate the hard work your doing in making a great game.

I just saw the want to add the ability to "Snap" in the game I can not support this enough. Being OCD I like my lights and shelves perfect so this function will help. One thing I've noticed is the stockers if my shelves and storage is full will just hold on to the box and not do anything. If we could have them toss the box on the ground so they can keep working that would be nice. I also don't see the point in cars. I know its cheaper to go to the other stores but I don't have time. If I could get a discount for ordering a bunch of stuff from their store that would be helpful. I haven't gotten the DLC yet but it's only a matter of time and can't wait to see all the new stuff from that. So if your still sitting on the fence may I recommend a stress free cozy game!! Buy This Now you can thank me latter.

I played Supermarket Simulator throughout its beta and absolutely loved it. It was one of those rare indie games that I couldn’t wait to recommend. The gameplay loop was addictive, the steady updates were exciting, and I was looking forward to supporting the full release.

Unfortunately, the launch completely changed my opinion.

Instead of simply releasing the finished game, the developer immediately introduced seven paid DLC packs, ranging from $1.99 to $6.99, that add nothing but product skins. Individually they may seem inexpensive, but together they create the feeling that content has been carved out to be sold separately on day one.

For a game that built its reputation during Early Access, this left a bad taste in my mouth. It feels less like supporting an indie developer and more like the beginning of a microtransaction strategy that I simply don’t want to encourage.

The core game is still enjoyable, but the monetization has fundamentally changed how I view it. What was once a must-buy has become an avoid for me—not because of the gameplay, but because of the direction the developer chose to take.

I hope the developer reconsiders this approach, because there is still a great game underneath it.

This game had a great foundation that also had the advantage of huge social media exposure, only to be held back by a dev "team" with slimy behavior. Very disappointing.

This game has big potential, but right now I can't recommend it yet. IMO it is very close to being recommended though:

Good: I don't really know what it is that kept me going to store level 27, it does scratch some kind of itch that is hard to explain. It's satisfying when you see a customer puts 6 bags of dishwasher tablets (high profit) on the conveyor belt, beep beep beep, sorting the coins, giving change, closing the register and just walk around the store to check how it's going. That's fun for a few hours. Also good: no bugs as far as I can see.

Bad: The restockers are doing a mighty fine job now, that's a big help. However, in order to keep track of your stock you have to constantly be walking up and down the store and storage room, remember where products are placed and trying to memorize that when you walk up to the computer to order stuff. Ideally, this would all be visible in one screen on the computer. When a rack is empty the restockers will put any product in its place, making you lose track of what is where.

Ugly: At this point I see little point in progressing any further, I won't unlock anything new that makes things more fun, only more complicated. Expanding the store and products would only give more headaches trying to keep stock up to date, without an increase of fun anywhere.
The atmosphere is very dead, it gives off a liminal space-vibe which is fun for a few hours but then you're like what am I doing here. There is little feedback from the robotic customers, even less from your cashier or restockers.

What I'd like to see: social interactions, questions from customers, adapted behaviour of customers in relation to prices, store layout - the staff should have more depth, skillpoints, different wages, training.
Marketing to affect customers (discounts, coupons, posters, in-store marketing). The ambiance should be a part as well, with plants and proper lighting to increase customer satisfaction. You could have the option to become a low-priced store with little ambiance while still drawing customers to the low prices, or you can make it a fancy store with marble floors and jack up prices, just to see that you will be visited more by customers in fancy clothes, paying higher prices. Play music in your store at a price to draw in more customers etc. etc. etc. - the options are endless.

Right now there is also no competition, no insight in how your prices affect the overall turnover or profit, no clear way to see what your choices actually have for effect.

At this point it is more Restocking+cashier simulator, it could be so much more. The core gameplay needs to be more fun. I'm hoping the updates will keep coming regularly because I think this game could be absolutely wonderful.

There's a good core gameplay loop here, but it's in need of some serious refinement.

1) There are too many annoying bugs.  Nothing game breaking that I've found, but there's a couple in particular that irritate me.  Like occasionally you'll get a customer delivery order with no notification.  In this scenario, bringing up the bag shows the incorrect number of delivery orders in progress.  You can still fill the order, but you need to be constantly checking to make sure one didn't slip in.  Also, there's a bug with the car where about 2/3 of the time, putting a box in the trunk also causes you to enter the car, which is *really* annoying when you're trying to load up a bunch of boxes, which you'll have to do because......

2) The game gets *very* tedious about 10 hours in.  Once you unlock a vehicle, you'll realize that you effectively *need* to get your products from the other stores around town, because they all sell goods at half their market value.  This is the only realistic way to make money after a certain point because your employee and bill costs get too high to manage on the margins afforded by ordering your goods online.  The problem is, getting goods from these stores is insanely time-inefficient.  There's no way to create a meaningful shopping list to take with you (you *can* use the product scanner to sorta create one, but it doesn't work at the other stores so you're constantly flipping to and from it just to look at whatever you added to it).  It effectively becomes a memory game for what you need to get, and beyond that, the vehicles only fit so much, so you end up spending 10-15 minutes at the start of every day driving back and forth to these stores, which completely invalidates the product scanner, which was one of the best things they added to the release game.

3) The game forces you to automate away your agency.  I know a lot of people are gonna say "well, just don't do that then" and you'd be right, if it weren't for the delivery orders that only you can do.  None of the other jobs (save cleaning) can be left unattended when you're doing multiple deliveries per day.  You will need, at the bare minimum, one cashier, one assistant, one security guard, and every restocker the game will let you unlock.  Otherwise your store will cease to function while you're away.  I think a good fix for this, ironically, is to add another automated employee: the delivery driver who can do deliveries for you.  Then, rather than allowing the player to unlock as many employees as they want, instead have a max employee count that scales with level, and it's up to you to decide how to allocate those slots among the different employee types, leaving whatever task(s) the player finds most enjoyable for themselves.  More customization is more good.

4) Restockers are still really annoying sometimes.  I hate how you'll be trying to reorganize a shelf, and they'll come in and restock it before you can remove the tag, or fill a shelf before you can put stolen goods back onto it.  There needs to be a grace period after the player interacts with a shelf, or some way to temporarily lock a shelf, that will prevent restockers from getting in your way.

5) XP and money gain are way out of whack with one another.  You'll spend most of the game having a crazy excess of one while being severely bottlenecked by the other, creating long periods of mindless grinding before you can unlock new content, at which point the bottleneck will flip to the other resource, and the whole process will start anew.  Some progression smoothing is needed, or some kind of system that lets you turn XP gain into money gain, or vice versa.  Maybe some special kiosks around the store.  Like, maybe a lottery scratcher machine that takes some of the money customers would otherwise spend on products (meaning you don't get it), but gives you bonus XP when they buy scratchers.  Or an arcade cabinet that does the opposite, bonus money at the cost of XP.  Just something that would let the player customize their resource gains in some way.

6) The game is begging for a talent tree of some kind.  Supermarket Together has one, and while it's not perfect, it's certainly interesting.

I really love this game, BUT at it's current state I'll not play until there are improvements.

It pains me to see that improving the restocking is nowhere to be seen in the game's roadmap. 
That has to be one of the most frustrating parts of the game, IMO.

At first, you don't have many items to take care of and re-stock, but as your store grows and you start acquiring licenses, you basically need to have every single item in stock, otherwise customers won't find them and complain. 

When you acquire enough licenses, holy sh!t, the amount of buying and restocking that has to be done makes the game a burden: 

- Buy 10 boxes of whatever items. 
- Store all of them one at a time.

- Buy 10 boxes of whatever items. 
- Store all of them one at a time.

- Buy 10 boxes of whatever items. 
- Store all of them one at a time.

- Buy 10 boxes of whatever items. 
- Store all of them one at a time.

- Buy 10 boxes of whatever items. 
- Store all of them one at a time.

Ad infinitum

It usually takes me 10-20 minutes every day just restocking and I don't even have many licenses (2 or 3).
I refrain from doing anything else in the game like upgrading the store and acquiring more licenses, just because I think of the toll that managing that stock will have on me. It stops being fun after a while.

I really wish I could focus on expanding my product selection and expanding and organizing my store to my liking, but I spend most of my time restocking...

Dev, PLEASE make this a priority in your roadmap if other players feel the same way. Customization and making the store bigger is useless if you have to spend a real time hour every day just restocking.

There's a few ways I could see improvements in that area:

1. The re-stockers SHOULD BE ABLE TO pick up the boxes that have been bought and place them in the rack by themselves. This could be optional or an upgrade to the re-stockers, so that players can manage the stock themselves if they so desire.
2. There could be an auto buy feature, so that you can schedule item purchases for the next morning;
3. The limit of buying 10 boxes at a time makes no sense, unless that is for performance reasons;
4. Picking up a single box at a time, going to the street, then to the storage multiple times is really cumbersome. Maybe consider picking up multiple boxes at a time;
5. There could be a feature to buy the exact amount of boxes the racks are missing of a specific item.

There are just some of the things I can think of right now, but they would GREATLY improve the experience of the game and allow players to focus more on other aspects of the game.

- The NPC pathfinding crashes from time to time, or they just get stuck on something. There should be a timed reset on their actions to overthink whether they can complete the task they're attempting to do so this doesn't happen.

UPDATED REVIEW: 
Now that this game is fully released and I have doubled the amount of play time, I would like to update my review! 10/10 Love that the Devs have listened to several complaints and continue to work on this game and make improvements!

Pros: 
1) the graphics are super nice!
2) progress is slow but steady, making it SO addicting. 
3) you can purchase vehicles later on in the game, which then allows you to drive around to different shops where you can get stuff to restock your shop for HALF of the full cost you would pay to order items.
4) eventually you can unlock staffing features making it so you don't have to do everything on your own, and it's fairly cheap to hire/fire people!
5) bills start real low and take a while to get over $100 a day.
6) plenty of things to do while your shop is open!
7) the town huge but easy to navigate.
8) runs great even if you only meet the minimum requirements! 
9) controls are super easy to learn.
10) you can click on your staff to "boost" their productivity. Maximum is 6 boosts.
11) They've added the ability for multiple save files!

Cons: 
1) not much to do when the store is closed until you unlock the discount shops mentioned in the "pros" category.
2) the characters aren't able to be talked to; npc will just walk right through you and walls.
3) if you have Thieves enabled, you get MINIMUM of one per day, just not realistic and way too frequent.
4) the vehicles cost a LOT and all of them EXCEPT the pickup truck are useless.
5) every time you click on a staff member, it charges you $3 in game, so if you do maximum boost on one associate, you're spending $18 in game dollars.

Regardless of the cons, I've gotten some good hours of gameplay out of this and I love it. Will keep playing for sure, it's a great way to burn a few hours without even noticing!

Have a dream of designing and running your own supermarket? Well then [i]Supermarket Simulator[/i] is the game for you.

[h3]Gameplay & Features[/h3]

In this game you get to own your own supermarket, starting off with a small storefront that sells a limited supply of goods. You can expand your store eventually, design it the way you want, hire employees, restock the shelves and decide what you want to sell. 

There are eventually a lot of items you will be able to buy. As your store levels up you can purchase licenses to sell more products. Some will require special equipment like fridges so keep this in mind when picking your products. Once ordered your products immediately are delivered in boxes to the front of your store. You simply grab the box, open it and place the items where you want them. If you want to stock up on items for the future  you do have a storage room in a separate space off to the right of your store that you can buy items for as well such as storage racks. It is also expandable, like your store.

[h3]The Visuals & Audio[/h3]

Visually this game looks pretty good for a simulation game in early access and at its price point. I was really pleasantly surprised. You can walk around the block taking in the scene. When you walk around you really get the sense you're in a small neighbourhood running your own small store. 

The food items themselves are very well done. Clear and clean labels and the product packing is well done and readable. You can tell a lot of care went into the small details of the game to enhance your immersion.

The NPC’s like in most sims are okay. They do clip and you will see lots of duplicates. And they do have that common “deer in headlights” stare that you see a lot in sim games (even some triple A’s too-looking at you Starfield). But I expect most sim games put their focus primarily into the environment, the mechanics and the quality of life stuff.  

In terms of audio all the ambient sounds you expect to hear are well done. Like the beep of scanning items for example. For music you need to buy a speaker from the furniture shop. Then you can select what music you’d like to play in your store once purchased. It is your classic, instrumental type music that you hear in real life stores while shopping. I hope they add seasonal tracks when the holidays roll around. 

[h3]Early Access Wishlist[/h3]

* Update prices of items and see their quantities on your computer. To go around and check labels individually when you start expanding is pain.
* Allow us to snap our furniture pieces in place to line them up. Allow us to turn the snap option on and off so for some items you can place them freely if desired.  
* We need the ability to move products without a box. Or if a box is needed have it as a quick select option (a box dedicated to moving products around that we always have access to and fits ALL products)

[h3]Overall Experience[/h3]

To say I am impressed with a simulator game, in early access, to this point is an understatement. I have played many sims and most are pretty bad. The devs actually listen to feedback and post on the main menu what is upcoming and they are working on. 

It is refreshing to have a positive experience with a sim in early access when a lot of times you don’t get that experience in fully released ones. I got my copy on sale for $12 and honestly this is a really good price for the fun I am having. 

Is there much needed features, yes (see my wishlist section) but it is in early access so if you are not one who wants to contribute to the development of the game or finding issues then it is best to wait. But for those who love sim games and don’t mind early access there is still enough here to have some fun.

2. Buying items. There is no in game indication of what items you are low on besides just looking at your shelves. This is fine in the early game but the further you progress, the more items you have to keep track of. And worst of all, there is this stupid cap that doesnt let you buy more than 10 items. This doesnt sound so bad but in the end game, you can buy up to 80 items at a time. 

3. Items. All the store items come in boxes that help you restock everything. The only issue is these boxes are so frustrating to work with. They only carry upwards to 16 items when you can easily work with 100+ at a time. This makes you just go back and forth and back and forth to restock shelves. Also, whenever you buy things, It quite literally drops the boxes from the sky onto the street. 

4. Animations and Aeshetics. Honestly this one is a personal thing, The character models are not awful or bad, its just they seem really low resoultion and there are only like 10 different characters. The check out workers have awful animations and take such a long time to perform one checkout.

5. BUGS. This game is filled with SO MANY BUGS. The restockers break constantly, Customers just stand in your store forever. The game straight up randomly takes away your money. I have no clue why. One time I launched the game and it immediatly put me into the menu where you rename your store. It is super frustrating.

6. Bankruptcy. This is by far the worst one imo. It actually made me write this review in the first place. I had a high level store that was performing very well, until one night, i had negative 100 dollars. This was fine I thought. I had a ton of items and could easily make thousands the next day. But apparently. If you end the day with a negative amount of money. It will instantly bankrupt you and end the game. And then it automatically deletes your entire save and makes you start from the very beggining. There was NO indication that would happen and it was devestating. I lost SO much progress and it was awful

7. Other. There are a lot of other issues in this game that dont deserve their own section. So im just gonna list them here.

Lack of store interaction. (you cant really advertise or see the analytics of your store)
Decentives to progress (more items to keep track of)
Only 1 save file
Useless city
Ugly store location with no way to change it
Random price changes that dont really change anything
Incredibly slow workers
Cap of 8 workers. 4 checkouters, 4 restockers.
Incredibly expensive expansions
Ai art for the banner
and so much more I cant think of right now

I had a lot of fun with this game. It could probably use a bit more variety, especially in the later levels, and multiplayer is quite buggy still in the full release.

That being said, I likely won't be touching the game again. Someone managed to hack into active multiplayer lobbies and change the name of our store, and that of many others. When this was reported in their official discord server, all evidence was promptly deleted, and we were accused of trolling, ban-evading, and making the whole thing up. Then we were all banned in the discord server. Taking it to the unofficial subreddit, multiple posts were made about the issue, and once again everyone expressing concerns about the game's security were dismissed, and the devs made a public post accusing us once again of trolling/raiding. Even after a streamer captured live evidence of another round of hacking and posted it, they continued to say "there was no hack, the game is fine".

Now, two full days later, the devs have edited their original accusatory message to claim they were always looking into it and taking our concerns seriously, though they still claim that some people were trolling. 

Will they fix the security breach? Maybe. Is the breach a serious threat to our systems? We'll probably never know. However, what I do know, is that after being berated for several days for politely bringing up a serious security concern, I have no more interest in playing this game. I cannot in good conscience recommend the game, knowing that this is how the devs and their chosen moderators handle bugs and issues. Even now that they're acknowledging that there is an issue, they *still* refuse to admit that they tried to gaslight us and everyone else into thinking there was no hack. 

If the devs fix the issue and give a full apology for how the situation was handled (and no, simply unbanning us on discord is not enough), perhaps then I'll consider returning to the game. Until then, it's a no.

I actually do recommend this game. The reason I have opted to choose not recommended, is because the game is very bare bones right now.

Once you've satisfied that itch you get from the start of the new game, it can get old rather quickly with very few things to keep it spiced up and entertaining, as you begin to spend 30 minutes buying all new inventory, loading them into your storage, and micromanaging everything. I get that's the point of the game, but from a video game perspective with QOL, there should be some changes.

That, and the developer is a single person that doesn't update the game a ton. The entire month of April we only had 1 small update and that was it. So while there is a good sized roadmap that has some interesting things to it, I'm not sure how long it will take to reach those goals when it's a solo person. I'm not sure the developer even intends to bring help on board with it.

I would say wishlist it and come back in 6-12 months. By then, we should have some interesting concepts they plan on adding brought into the game by then. (security, shoplifting, self checkout, etc.)

This is a fun game, but there are many things that don't really make sense. 

- I think that the rewards do not align with profit. Many things costs a lot of money to do. I am seeing why there is such a low percentage rate of those getting steam achievements. The balance of reward and profit is off - it's really hard to obtain things unless you're are committed to playing this game for hours and hours. I think this would make many people give up on playing because it takes too long to do stuff. 

- I don't want to HAVE to paint the walls as an objective. This should be optional - or lower the cost of paint. Again, this is one of those unbalanced costs vs. what I am making in the game. $200 per paint bucket that doesn't even fill an entire wall. 

- On the cash register, the amount due back to customer is in a bright yellow font - it's really hard to read. They should make this portion of font in red or have some kind of black outline around the yellow - they should also make this bigger than the rest of the font. Not everyone is playing this on a giant monitor. I even have glasses on and it's hard to read. No one wants to see a neon yellow font. 

- In what world are cashiers typing the total into the card reader? It doesn't makes sense I have to use the "enter" button on the keyboard to confirm the transaction, but when I use the cash register, I have to use the "space bar". The flip-flop of keys is messy. They should remove having to enter the total and just have an "charge card" or "accept transaction/total" button instead. This will streamline motion of the game and I don't have to have tired hands entering numbers. It's really annoying. The amount is already on the screen next to the card reader. This is meaningless task and takes away from a fully functioning game. 

- There should be an option to give the stocker and the cashier a raise to work faster. This is also unbalanced. 

- Saving money in this game is difficult with the unbalanced rewards to purchase AND keeping the shelves stocked.

- There are no instructions on what to do with online orders? It just suddenly started to happen in the game. There's no instructions where I am supposed to set it in the game once I have filled the bag. I have no idea what I am supposed to be doing with it? So I just ignored the delivery orders - but the sound effect that goes off is annoying. There should be an option to shut off the pick-up/delivery bag thing - just like any grocery store would chose to offer or not.

- The top left corner of the game will alert you to spoiled food - but for some reason it pops up on the screen for only seconds and it's gone. It's so small and unreadable. What's the point? Maybe in the price section on the computer it can show when stuff will spoil ---- or maybe a drop down box of "notification history" on the top left corner so I can go back and see these? Because suddenly there will rotten food on the floor and I don't know why. I am still unsure if this from spoiled food or just a 'messy' store.

There are some other annoying things I can't think of right now. But I am getting the vibe whom ever is making this game is either being realllllyyyyyyy stubborn about certain functions, or they are are having a hard time with the development of this game as a whole. 

I do really appreciate the game hasn't crashed on me once. Even though I save the game religiously, just in case.

I have put 500 soul-sucking hours into this game, and it took me a year and a half of grinding (without exploits) to get every achievement. 

I idled this game all the time while restockers worked to put product back on the shelves and put away the million boxes I had to buy every 1-2 in-game days. I spent entire weekends playing this game to grind out the store expansions. Could I have done it faster if I used exploits or mods? Duh. 

I only got this game after liking some similar Roblox games, it was fun up until level 40. Basically, you buy all the product licenses and there's nothing new after that except rearranging the store every time you buy expansions so it looks less dumb? When I tell you that my heart dropped when they added MORE store expansions and NO new product licenses -- 

Would suck less if the boxes didn't appear on the sidewalk and if your restockers weren't the slow cousins of the TMNT (for some reason, tipping them $3 is enough to make them lightly jog about 0.05mph faster for 30 seconds). 

I wanted so badly to have never bought this game, but my brain would NOT let me leave this game unfinished, and so I idled while I worked, while I cleaned, cooked meals, sat in calls, read books, anything at all to not have to sit here and watch these restockers trudge around for thirty minutes. My hours are def inflated because of this, but I could not be bothered sitting there and watching them walk around for 20-30 mins to jump up and restock once they were finally done. 

The enjoyable part of the game was earlier on when you were actually getting new products and items, but you reach a point where you never get any more customers, it just caps, and it's sooo slow to accumulate money. Averaging 4500 per day if I was keeping warehouse fully stocked before each day. When each expansion eventually costs 160,000, and there's no reason for the store to get any larger, it's just a grind of multiple in-game days to try and save up so that you can spend even more of your meager savings on rent every single day. 

My boyfriend thinks I have a problem for working a retail job on Steam after working 12 hour shifts. I clearly do. There are free games that accomplish this better than this one, and it's obviously not getting any new products to make it feel at least a bit less repetitive. God bless anybody who wastes as much time as I did playing this o7

So I've played 41 hours, and I'm at level 40, and you're probably wondering, how on earth can I sink that much time into a game at such a reasonable price and not recommend it?  And the answer is - because it became a timesink long before level 40.  I would really prefer to play this type of game without mods, so I haven't played the game with any.  Without, there are still too many little irritations that add up right now:

1. lack of snap to grid, making shelving VERY hard to place
2. slow employees with no opportunity to train them for higher speeds
3. Restocking sucks
a) you are the only person who can order, you cannot order after 9pm, you can only order 10 items at a time, you can only carry one box at a time, and each box has to be thrown into the garbage can - you guessed it! - one at a time.  At level 40 even with far fewer licenses than I technically *could* buy, each in-game day was turning into stocking and stocking and stocking and stocking and stocking and buying and buying and stocking and stocking and buying and stocking and... then it's a 5 minute or so day where you can't engage with customers through the till at all anymore because you need to keep stocking and stocking and...
b) TINY icons. If I'm trying to read a label on the upper shelf I can't see the image, it's too small.
c) There's no 'lock' function for shelf assignments so if you misclick, that shelf is now the shelf for the things you're carrying, and to get it back you have to remove the offending item, drop it, get a new box of the correct item and shove it in just to 'undo' the incorrect labelling.  But do it fast, because the moment your slow af stockers smell a mostly-empty mislabelled shelf they will rush over with the speed of greyhounds to start filling it up with stock.
d) No ability to move stock without boxes.  Did you just misclick and add an item out of a full box to the shelf then one of those butthead stockers run in and fill up the shelf with THEIR box and then THROW OUT that box so that now you are unable to remove that stock from the wrong shelf until you manage to empty a box that is the right size (good luck remembering which it was)? Yeah, me too.
e) Inventory management, oh my god. They will pull random boxes and half fill a shelf and put the box back, then pick a different box next time, NO idea why but it sure does throw off how many boxes I can order vs how many I should be able to.  And unfortunately instructing them to use empty racks doesn't work - instead of using UNASSIGNED racks as I would expect them to, they use just any old rack. So I kept running back to a perfectly sorted section to find any old shit piled up in the blank spots. The only way to check how much you need for inventory is to run back and forth to the shelves and the computer because for some reason your brand new supermarket with fancy self checkouts doesn't keep a digital inventory.

Despite the above I HAVE played 40 hours.  This is an excellent start but it just needs more polish so that progression doesn't turn into a game of stock clerk simulator.
